I reviewed the whole file, lines 1–116, using only the simp-interface rubric. I did not open any related source files, so this rests on the target text alone.

The only simp-related content is the three `@[simps]`/`@[simps!]` attributes on `structuredArrowRightwardsOpEquivalence.functor`, `structuredArrowRightwardsOpEquivalence.inverse` and `structuredArrowRightwardsOpEquivalence`. They generate projection lemmas for auxiliary data. The unit and counit isos are `Iso.refl _`, so those projections reduce trivially. I saw nothing that would loop or compete with another rule.

The other declarations are instances and the iff `guitartExact_op_iff`. This iff has `w.op.GuitartExact` on the left and `w.GuitartExact` on the right. It is proved by an explicit decomposition and is not tagged `@[simp]`. The `w.op` form could plausibly be simp-normalised, but I found no uses in the file showing a practical gain. The rubric also warns against adding simp attributes only because a statement looks simple.

Uncertainty: I did not check downstream uses of the generated simp lemmas, and I could not run Lean.
